papers.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
papers.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysoz
papers.summary: Researchers tracked one person's gut microbiome at 51 time points over 3.6 years, building time-point-specific metabolic models from metagenomic data and using flux balance analysis to predict microbial metabolic activity. They then compared these predictions and microbial abundances against clinical inflammation markers (CRP, lactoferrin, calprotectin). This deep single-subject design links microbiome composition and predicted metabolism to episodic colonic inflammation.

papers.title: An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To characterize systemic transcriptomic signatures and identify candidate hub genes associated with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) in peripheral blood using an integrative systems-biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies an integrative systems-biology approach to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets for LSCC. The work highlights the value of combining transcriptomics with network analysis to detect systemic signals beyond the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.
papers.abstract: The distinction between primary and secondary metabolism has long provided a useful conceptual and pedagogical framework in biochemistry, particularly in plant sciences, but it increasingly fails as a literal description of how metabolites are produced and function. Pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulatory mechanisms, transport systems, and recycling routes, while metabolites conventionally assigned to different categories can contribute to growth, signaling, defense, nutrient acquisition, structure, or stress responses depending on context. Here, we review the historical origins of th
papers.summary: This review argues that the traditional distinction between primary and secondary metabolism in plants is conceptually outdated. It shows that metabolic pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulation, transport, and recycling, and that metabolites can serve growth, signaling, defense, or stress roles depending on context. The authors call for a unified metabolic perspective instead of the primary-secondary dichotomy.

papers.title: Hierarchical Gene Regulatory Networks Improve Gene Prioritization in TWAS by Constraining Trans-Regulatory Search.
papers.abstract: Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) link genetically regulated expression (GReX) to complex traits and provide a widely used framework for prioritizing candidate genes from genome-wide association study (GWAS)signals. However, most TWAS models focus primarily on local cis-regulation, whereas distal trans-regulation remains difficult to incorporate because of the large genomic search space. Here we present GRNTWAS (Gene regulatory network-guided transcriptome-wide association study), a framework that incorporates hierarchical gene regulatory networks (GRNs) to define a biologically co
papers.summary: The authors introduce GRNTWAS, a framework that incorporates hierarchical gene regulatory networks to constrain the search for trans-regulatory effects in transcriptome-wide association studies. By restricting the distal regulatory search space using biological network structure, the method improves gene prioritization from GWAS signals compared to standard cis-focused TWAS approaches.

papers.title: [Progress, challenges, and strategies of biomanufacturing with non-food feedstocks].
papers.abstract: Biomanufacturing serves as the important component and key technological pathway of the bioeconomy, and the utilization of non-food feedstocks represents a pivotal path for its rapid development. This review systematically summarizes the research progress and key challenges of biomanufacturing with three major categories of non-food feedstocks: lignocellulose, C1 compounds, and organic wastes. For lignocellulose, technological breakthroughs and economic bottlenecks in pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, co-utilization of mixed sugars, lignin valorization, and consolidated bioprocessing are cri
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This review surveys the progress and challenges of using non-food feedstocks—lignocellulose, C1 compounds (e.g., CO2, methanol), and organic wastes—for biomanufacturing. It highlights technical breakthroughs and economic bottlenecks in pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, mixed-sugar co-utilization, lignin valorization, and consolidated bioprocessing, and discusses strategies to advance industrial adoption.

papers.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the underlying interactions through which transcription factors (TFs) regulate genes. Based on gene expression data, existing GRN inference approaches generally fall into two categories: graph-based methods, which model the GRN as a whole graph, and pairwise-based methods, which decompose the GRN into individual TF-target gene pairs for modeling. However, each approach exhibits limitations that are precisely the strengths of its counterpart. Graph-based methods tend to overfit due to their reliance on a single training graph, whereas pairwise-based metho
papers.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid approach that combines graph-based and pairwise-based learning to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data. The method aims to overcome the overfitting tendency of graph-based methods and the limited global context of pairwise methods by leveraging the strengths of both paradigms. The result is a more robust GRN inference framework that captures both local TF-target relationships and global network structure.

papers.title: M-SCAN: Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks for Genome-Scale Flux Inference in Pan-Cancer Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism reflects both recurrent tumour programmes and tissue-specific constraints, but transcriptome analyses do not directly estimate metabolic reaction fluxes. We developed Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks (M-SCAN), a reproducible workflow for sample-wise genome-scale flux inference across heterogeneous cancer cohorts.
papers.summary: M-SCAN is a reproducible workflow that infers genome-scale metabolic reaction fluxes for individual tumor samples across heterogeneous pan-cancer cohorts, addressing the gap where transcriptome data alone cannot directly estimate metabolic flux. It combines multi-scale constrained analysis of metabolic networks to capture both recurrent tumor programs and tissue-specific metabolic constraints.

papers.title: Protocol for thermodynamic analysis of genome-scale metabolic models using dGbyG and ThermoInfer.
papers.abstract: Accurate thermodynamic information can be used to improve the quality of genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs). Here, we present a computational protocol that integrates the dGbyG and ThermoInfer algorithms for thermodynamic analysis of GEMs. We describe steps for setting up the computational environment, implementing a workflow for predicting standard Gibbs free energy changes using dGbyG, and performing thermodynamic flux balance analysis with ThermoInfer to identify thermodynamically inconsistent reactions. We illustrate the workflow using the Yeast9-GEM model as an example. For complete det
papers.summary: This protocol describes a computational workflow that combines two algorithms, dGbyG and ThermoInfer, to add thermodynamic constraints to genome-scale metabolic models. dGbyG predicts standard Gibbs free energy changes for reactions, and ThermoInfer then performs thermodynamic flux balance analysis to flag reactions that are thermodynamically inconsistent. The authors demonstrate the workflow on the Yeast9-GEM model, providing step-by-step guidance for setting up the environment and running the analysis.

papers.title: The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.
papers.abstract: Chronic degenerative diseases are traditionally explained in terms of disease-specific initiating lesions and molecular pathways. Although this approach has substantially advanced understanding of disease mechanisms, it does not fully explain why biologically diverse disorders often converge on persistent states marked by chronic inflammation, impaired repair, altered nutrient sensing, reduced adaptive flexibility, and incomplete recovery after the initiating insult subsides. This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS), a systems-level framework that distinguishes disease init
papers.summary: This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS) as a systems-level framework to explain why biologically diverse chronic diseases converge on persistent states of chronic inflammation, impaired repair, and reduced adaptive flexibility. The framework distinguishes disease-initiating lesions from the self-sustaining stress state that maintains pathology after the original insult subsides, offering a unifying conceptual model for chronic disease persistence.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: Researchers built the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, using a new reconstruction approach that incorporates experimentally determined nutrient requirements. The model improves on earlier automatically generated drafts and enables analysis of the strain's metabolic secretions. This provides a more accurate computational tool for studying LGG metabolism in industrial and health contexts.

papers.title: Meta-finetuning foundation models for generalizable biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes.
papers.abstract: Biological image segmentation is essential for analyzing cellular structures, yet labeled data are often labor-intensive and expensive to obtain, which limits conventional deep learning models in low-data settings. Building upon the bi-level meta-finetuning formulation introduced in BLO-SAM, we evaluate MetaTune for adapting foundation models to biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes. MetaTune separates the model's learnable components into meta-parameters, which enhance generalization, and non-meta parameters, which focus on task-specific adaptation. Through an iterative, two
papers.summary: MetaTune adapts foundation models for biological image segmentation when labeled data are extremely scarce by splitting model parameters into meta-parameters that improve generalization and non-meta parameters that handle task-specific adaptation, using an iterative bi-level meta-finetuning scheme. Building on the BLO-SAM formulation, the work evaluates this approach in ultra-low-data regimes, aiming to make segmentation models more generalizable across biological imaging tasks without large annotated datasets.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating how accurately the resulting network structures capture causal relationships between genes. This addresses a gap in available software for both Bayesian network inference and structural causal assessment in single-cell GRN analysis.

papers.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
papers.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.summary: This review discusses how computational (in-silico) methods can be combined with traditional ethnopharmacological knowledge to accelerate herbal drug discovery. It argues that integrating traditional disease classification with modern computational tools can help identify bioactive phytochemicals and clarify their mechanisms of action, addressing a key barrier to clinical translation.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their microscopy images, without needing shared molecular features or prior annotations. It enables the creation of unified multi-modal spatial datasets by reliably registering slides from different spatial transcriptomics technologies, tissues, and resolutions, performing comparably to established uni-modal alignment tools.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Network Modeling of Lipid Metabolism in Brassica juncea: A Roadmap for Precision Oil Engineering.
papers.abstract: Brassica juncea (Indian mustard) is an economically important oilseed crop, but high erucic acid in traditional seed oils and elevated glucosinolates in seed meal remain important quality-improvement targets. Its allotetraploid genome, developmental regulation, and environmental responses complicate the prediction and engineering of lipid-related traits. This narrative review synthesizes experimentally supported findings on fatty acid biosynthesis, triacylglycerol assembly, and genetic regulation in B. juncea, and distinguishes these findings from evidence transferred from Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes experimentally supported knowledge on fatty acid biosynthesis, triacylglycerol assembly, and genetic regulation in Brassica juncea, and proposes a systems biology and network modeling framework for precision oil engineering. It emphasizes distinguishing direct B. juncea evidence from inferences transferred from Arabidopsis, given the crop's allotetraploid genome and complex developmental and environmental regulation. The work serves as a roadmap for improving oil quality traits such as erucic acid content and glucosinolate levels.

papers.title: Integrated Pan-Cancer Profiling of the Human Lysine Deacetylase Superfamily Identifies SIRT7 as a Central Regulator of Genome Stability and Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Lysine deacetylases (KDACs) are central regulators of chromatin organization, transcription, metabolism, DNA repair, and cellular signaling, yet their molecular and clinical landscape across human cancers has not been systematically defined. Here, we performed the first comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of the complete human lysine deacetylase superfamily by integrating transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical datasets across The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Systematic analyses of all 18 human deacetylases revealed extensive but highly heterogeneous patterns of dysregulation, demonstrating
papers.summary: This study provides the first comprehensive pan-cancer analysis of all 18 human lysine deacetylases using TCGA data, revealing widespread but heterogeneous dysregulation across cancer types. Through integrated transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical analyses, the authors identify SIRT7 as a central regulator of genome stability and cancer progression, highlighting it as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information.
papers.summary: This paper compares interventional causal structure learning algorithms for inferring gene regulatory networks, evaluating how different methods leverage intervention data to improve causal identifiability. It provides a systematic benchmark of these algorithms, highlighting trade-offs in accuracy and applicability for gene regulation studies.

papers.title: Dolphin semen metabolome characterization and relationships with sperm quality.
papers.abstract: Identification and quantification of metabolites in semen can augment assisted reproductive technologies by indicating reproductive health and fertility. Species-specific semen metabolites associated with improved semen quality remain largely unknown in exotic species due to limited sample availability.
papers.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
papers.summary: This study characterizes the metabolome of dolphin semen and examines its relationship with sperm quality metrics. By identifying and quantifying seminal metabolites, the authors aim to find species-specific biomarkers that could inform reproductive health assessment and assisted reproduction in this exotic species. The work addresses a gap in knowledge about semen metabolites in non-model marine mammals.

papers.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a su
papers.summary: The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells, covering over 2,100 reactions. Using these models, they identified 28 enzyme-mediated metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient cells, 24 of which map to known or approved drugs. Independent DepMap data supported the predictions, demonstrating that multi-omics-constrained kinetic modeling can quantify pathway rewiring and prioritize therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.
papers.abstract: Gravitropism redirects plant organ growth by converting gravity perception into asymmetric growth initiated in endodermal statocytes. Although the C2H2-type zinc finger transcription factor SHOOT GRAVITROPISM 5 (SGR5), also known as INDETERMINATE DOMAIN 15 (IDD15), is essential for shoot gravitropism, the transcriptional mechanisms linking gravity perception to directional growth remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-nucleus RNA sequencing to build a transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis stem and identify the endodermal gene regulatory network controlling gravitropism. The authors show that the transcription factor SGR5/IDD15 acts within endodermal statocytes to link gravity perception to asymmetric growth, providing a cell-type-resolved view of how plants redirect stem growth in response to gravity.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.
papers.abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of
papers.summary: This paper proposes "Longevitomics," a conceptual framework that integrates genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping, and AI into a unified systems science of healthy longevity. It defines the "Longevitome" as the dynamic multi-layered architecture underlying long life, arguing that studying these layers in isolation has limited explanatory power. The work is primarily a perspective/framework paper rather than an empirical study.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira grown at host-like temperature (37°C) upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that these bacteria rely mainly on fatty acids and have limited glucose use. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may reflect adaptation to the mammalian host environment.

papers.title: Network inference at single-cell resolution reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in limb evolution.
papers.abstract: How changes in conserved developmental genetic programs contribute to morphological evolution remains poorly understood, particularly in non-conventional model species. Here, we combine single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility profiling with cross-species label transfer and gene regulatory network inference to compare mouse and pig limb development. Our analyses identify broadly conserved cellular organization but discrete divergence in HOX-, FGF- and SHH-regulated programs. FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds phenocopies the distal expansion of pig GREM1 expression, while altered
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study compares limb development between mice and pigs using single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility, combined with gene regulatory network inference. It finds that while cellular organization is broadly conserved, specific HOX, FGF, and SHH regulatory programs diverge, and that FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds mimics the distal expansion of GREM1 seen in pigs. The work reveals multilayered buffering mechanisms that may allow developmental programs to diverge without disrupting overall limb morphology.

papers.title: Stochasticity in Metabolism: Oxidative Stress Response Phenotypes As Emergent Consequences of Network Topology.
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. Traditional ROS modeling has been confined to small ODE frameworks limited by kinetic-parameter scarcity. Here, we recast ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis (FBA) optimization problem using COBRA and CPLEX, augmenting the Escherichia coli iJO1366 genome-scale model with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions, targeting three ROS species: hydroxyl radicals, superoxide, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). We also fo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors extend the E. coli genome-scale metabolic model iJO1366 with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions to simulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) dynamics using flux-balance analysis rather than traditional ODE modeling. This recasts ROS handling as an optimization problem, enabling genome-scale mechanistic study of oxidative stress without requiring scarce kinetic parameters. The approach reveals how oxidative stress response phenotypes can emerge from network topology and stochasticity.

papers.title: Predicted Metabolic Potential of Citrobacter farmeri and Enterobacter cloacae from Unhatched Chelonia mydas Eggs: A Genome-Scale Extension.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives:Citrobacter farmeri and Enterobacter cloacae are opportunistic Enterobacteriaceae recovered from unhatched Chelonia mydas eggs, but their secondary metabolite and metabolic potential remain unresolved. This study examines which predicted differences between one isolate of each taxon are specific to the isolates and which are shared with public genomes of the same species. Methods: antiSMASH v7.1.0, KofamScan/KEGG-Decoder module profiling (178 modules) with BLASTP verification, and curated CarveMe v1.6.6 genome-scale metabolic modeling were applied to the draft genomes of
papers.summary: This study used genome mining tools (antiSMASH, KofamScan/KEGG modules, and CarveMe metabolic modeling) to compare the predicted secondary metabolite and metabolic potential of one Citrobacter farmeri and one Enterobacter cloacae isolate from unhatched green sea turtle eggs against public genomes of the same species. The authors distinguish isolate-specific predictions from species-shared features, providing a genome-scale extension of prior characterization of these opportunistic Enterobacteriaceae.

papers.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
papers.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from lab to field scale for soil bioremediation. It integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify barriers limiting field performance, rather than merely cataloging remediation processes. The authors propose evidence-based design principles for engineering plant-microbe-soil consortia.

papers.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.
papers.summary: The authors present scPhyloGRN, a method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by explicitly incorporating the lineage topology (cellular phylogeny) among individual cells. This addresses the confounding of cell-state and shared-ancestry expression patterns, using developmental context to guide gene-level regulatory inference.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.
papers.summary: This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging mouse cochlea, tracking how different cell types change across age. It identifies two phases of age-related inflammation (inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication and gene regulatory network analyses with bulk validation, providing a molecular timeline for age-related hearing loss.

papers.title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. Strain-specific GSMMs clustered by clonal complex (CC): in all nine CCs with ≥ 2 isolates the mean within-CC Jaccard distance was smaller than the mean between-CC distance; across all strain pairs the med
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed genome-scale metabolic models for 86 Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates and found that the models cluster by clonal complex, meaning strains from the same lineage have more similar metabolic capabilities than strains from different lineages. They validated this lineage-level metabolic structure against in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. This shows that metabolic model structure carries phylogenetic signal and can distinguish bacterial lineages.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 correlate with semen quality in rams, using ejaculates from five animals assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis. The authors combined experimental expression measurements with gene regulatory network analysis to identify potential upstream regulators of protamine expression. The work links protamine gene expression to sperm motility in a livestock species and proposes candidate regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to resolve disagreements between methods more intelligently than picking one method or simple averaging.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. The authors identify 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEA proteins and describe their coordinated transcriptional regulation, providing a resource for understanding salt tolerance mechanisms in this resilient plant.

papers.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell multiomics data to map the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis, revealing cellular and molecular changes underlying disease pathogenesis. The work provides a comprehensive atlas of cell-cell communication between epithelial and stromal compartments, identifying potential drivers of chronic inflammation.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using a computational genome-scale metabolic model tailored to endothelial cells, the authors predicted and then experimentally validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization during angiogenesis. This previously overlooked transporter supports biomass synthesis in proliferating endothelial cells, linking glutamine metabolism to blood vessel formation.

papers.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
papers.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for the plant pathogen Xylella fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The manually curated consensus model, iXfcore, was used to predict metabolic capabilities and identify putative conserved biochemical features of the species. This provides a resource for studying a fastidious pathogen whose metabolism was previously poorly characterized.

papers.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode
papers.summary: This study integrates a genome-scale metabolic model of Rhodopseudomonas palustris with machine learning to explore the multidimensional design space for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production. The hybrid framework identifies cost-efficient metabolic and operational strategies that would be impractical to find experimentally. It offers a computational route to lowering substrate and operational costs for microbial bioplastic production.

papers.title: A pathogen-free citrus model recapitulates Huanglongbing-associated molecular and physiological reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a devastating citrus disease associated with "Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus", but the contribution of host-driven processes to disease development remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a pathogen-free system to determine whether chloroplast dysfunction can reproduce key molecular and physiological features of HLB. Using Citrus tristeza virus-mediated silencing of phytoene desaturase (PDS) and δ-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALAD), we simultaneously disrupted carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis in Citrus macrophylla. Chloroplast dysfunction induced foli
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: The authors created a pathogen-free citrus model by silencing two chloroplast biosynthesis genes (PDS and ALAD) using a virus vector, disrupting carotenoid and chlorophyll production in Citrus macrophylla. This chloroplast dysfunction reproduced key molecular and physiological features of Huanglongbing (HLB), suggesting that host-driven chloroplast failure—rather than the pathogen alone—contributes substantially to disease development. The system provides a tractable platform for studying HLB mechanisms without requiring the unculturable pathogen.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.
papers.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold tremendous promise for disease modeling, drug discovery, and cardiac regenerative therapies. However, the immature phenotype of hPSC-CMs remains a major barrier limiting their translational utility. Here, we performed integrated multi-omic profiling to identify molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with hPSC-CM maturation during long-term culture. hPSC-CMs were cultured for 113 days and analyzed using metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics across progressive stages of maturation. Long-term culture induced
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) over 113 days of long-term culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with maturation. The multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs that could help overcome the immature phenotype limiting translational use of hPSC-CMs for disease modeling, drug discovery, and regenerative therapies.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review argues that TREM2 acts as a central molecular hub governing macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the simple M1/M2 classification. It emphasizes the importance of timing of TREM2 signaling and highlights therapeutic opportunities for targeting it in cardiovascular conditions.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This review argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill considerations are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms in toxicology.

papers.title: DiSCGRN: Sparse Nonstationary Gene Regulatory Network Inference with Continuous-Time Propagation and Discrete Switching.
papers.abstract: Background: Reconstructing time-varying gene regulatory networks is difficult when observations are sparse, sampling intervals differ, and the timing of network changes is unknown. We aimed to jointly estimate stage-specific networks and determine whether expression time courses support a regulatory change. Methods: We developed DiSCGRN to estimate sparse stage-specific networks using an affine differential-equation model with matrix-exponential propagation over the actual sampling intervals. Stage boundaries were selected by penalized comparison of single- and two-stage models, with threshold
papers.summary: DiSCGRN is a new computational method for reconstructing gene regulatory networks that change over time, even when expression data are sparse and sampled at irregular intervals. It models expression dynamics with differential equations propagated over actual sampling times and uses a penalized statistical test to decide whether the data support a single network or a switch between two stage-specific networks. The approach jointly estimates sparse stage-specific networks and detects the timing of regulatory changes.

papers.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. Duodenal transcriptomics from the Study of Environmental Enteropathy and Malnutrition (SEEM; 52 children with EED, 24 contr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used genome-scale metabolic modeling to compare duodenal transcriptomics from children with environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) against maternal plasma proteomes linked to adverse fetal growth. The authors found an overlapping amino acid metabolic signature across two independent cohorts, suggesting that some of the metabolic features attributed to acquired pediatric intestinal pathology may instead reflect growth restriction originating in utero.

papers.title: Systems Biology and Machine Learning Reveal Oxidative Stress Hubs and Therapeutic Targets in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that oxidative stress is involved in its pathophysiology. This study explored oxidative stress-related mechanisms in IBS-D and screened potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrative bioinformatics analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates bioinformatics and machine learning to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes and candidate diagnostic biomarkers in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D). It proposes oxidative stress pathways as potential therapeutic targets, though the findings are based on computational analysis of existing datasets.

papers.title: BoolFunc-EA: A Boolean-evolutionary approach for accurate inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Network inference is the process of discovering genetic information from time-series data. The inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series data represents a significant challenge in bioinformatics. Despite the development of many Boolean network inference methods, most struggle with scalability as they impose restrictions on regulatory genes for each target gene. Other methods suffer from local optimum issues or are unable to compute the exact mutual information between a regulatory gene and its target gene. To resolve these issues, we present a novel method referred to as BoolFunc-
papers.summary: BoolFunc-EA introduces a Boolean-evolutionary algorithm for inferring gene regulatory networks from time-series expression data, aiming to overcome scalability limits, local optima, and inaccurate mutual information estimates that affect existing Boolean network methods. The approach combines Boolean function learning with evolutionary search to identify regulatory relationships without imposing strict limits on the number of regulators per target gene. It is presented as a more accurate inference method for time-series gene expression data.

papers.title: Genome-scale mathematical model of cannabis glandular trichome metabolism and identification of a missing link in terpenoid biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: Cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.) glandular trichomes (GTs) are specialized structures on female inflorescences that serve as the primary sites for the biosynthesis and storage of metabolites responsible for potency and aroma, including cannabinoids, terpenoids, flavonoids, stilbenoids, phenolic amides, and volatile compounds. Despite substantial advances in cannabis biochemistry, uncertainties remain regarding key metabolic processes, including the biosynthetic origin of hexanoyl-CoA, the precursor supplying the cannabinoid side chain, and the formation of certain terpenoids such as 1,8-cineole.
papers.summary: The authors built a genome-scale mathematical model of cannabis glandular trichome metabolism, integrating known biochemistry to simulate the production of cannabinoids, terpenoids, and other specialized metabolites. Using the model, they identify a missing enzymatic link in terpenoid biosynthesis (specifically for compounds like 1,8-cineole) and clarify the metabolic origin of hexanoyl-CoA, the precursor for the cannabinoid side chain. This provides a computational framework for guiding future metabolic engineering and biochemical validation in cannabis.

papers.title: Transcriptome-Based, Genome-Scale Metabolic Modeling of Haemonchus contortus during Development and between Sexes.
papers.abstract: Parasitic nematodes undergo developmental transitions between external and host-associated environments, yet the accompanying changes in metabolic capacity remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed HaeconGEM, a genome-scale metabolic model of the blood-feeding nematode Haemonchus contortus. HaeconGEM v1 comprises 1,420 genes and 11,873 reactions. We integrated transcriptomic data from the egg, the L1 to L3 larval stages, female and male L4 larvae, and adult females and males to generate 8 transcriptome-constrained models. These models shared a broad set of metabolic functions but differed
papers.summary: The authors built HaeconGEM, a genome-scale metabolic model for the parasitic nematode Haemonchus contortus, containing 1,420 genes and 11,873 reactions. By integrating transcriptomic data across developmental stages (egg through adult) and both sexes, they generated eight context-specific models that reveal stage- and sex-specific differences in metabolic capacity. This provides a computational framework for understanding how this blood-feeding parasite adapts its metabolism during development and between males and females.

papers.title: Dry eye disease beyond tear deficiency: inflammation, biomarkers, genetics and precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent multifactorial ocular surface disorder that is associated with instability of the tear film, hyperosmolarity, inflammation, and abnormality of the neurosensory epithelium. Previously thought of as a passive outcome of poor tear production, DED is now recognized as a complex and heterogenous disease involving multiple interacting pathophysiological mechanisms. Inflammation plays an important role in DED, with significant implications on visual performance and quality of life across the globe. Recent advances have improved our understanding of the molecular p
papers.summary: This review reframes dry eye disease as a heterogeneous, multifactorial condition driven by tear film instability, hyperosmolarity, inflammation, and neurosensory epithelial dysfunction rather than simply a tear production deficit. It surveys emerging molecular biomarkers, genetic contributors, and inflammatory pathways, and discusses how these could support precision medicine approaches to diagnosis and treatment. The emphasis is on integrating mechanistic insight into stratified, patient-specific clinical management.

papers.title: A deep network embedding and robust statistical framework for multi-omics integration in rare diseases: a case study in PMM2-CDG.
papers.abstract: Integrative analysis of multiomic datasets in rare diseases is often constrained by small-n cohorts, impeding the identification of robust and biologically meaningful disease mechanisms. We developed an end-to-end framework that combines multiomic integration, robust statistical inference and network representation learning to extract clinically relevant molecular signatures from limited sample sizes. The framework prioritizes informative omic layers using Multiple Factor Analysis, identifies stable severity-associated features through stability selection and projects these features onto the h
papers.summary: The authors present an end-to-end computational framework that integrates multiple omics layers from small rare-disease cohorts using Multiple Factor Analysis for layer prioritization, stability selection for robust feature identification, and deep network embedding to project severity-associated features onto a network. They demonstrate the approach on PMM2-CDG, a rare congenital disorder of glycosylation, extracting clinically relevant molecular signatures despite limited sample sizes. The work offers a reusable pipeline for multi-omics integration in small-n settings.

papers.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the cellular heterogeneity of the ovarian ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), arguing that the disorder's clinical variability stems from diverse cell types and their interactions rather than a single endocrine or genetic defect. It highlights how recent single-cell and spatial technologies are beginning to resolve these cellular populations and connect them to clinical features. The paper frames PCOS as a multi-cellular, systems-level disorder and discusses implications for more personalized diagnosis and treatment.
